title: Client onboarding, risk profiling and suitability
objectives: Collect the right information and profile risk.
body_md:
A defensible recommendation rests on a documented profile.

## Onboarding

- KYC, PAN and contact details; the signed **client agreement**.
- Collect **financial information**: income, expenses, assets, liabilities, insurance, dependents.
- Collect **goals** with amounts, dates and priorities.

## Risk profile

| Dimension | Question |
|---|---|
| **Risk capacity** | How much loss can the client afford? (income stability, horizon, liabilities) |
| **Risk tolerance** | How much loss can the client stomach? (behaviour, experience) |
| **Risk required** | What return is needed to meet the goals? |

The **lower of capacity and tolerance** caps the risk taken, unless the goal can be met with less.

## Suitability

Each recommendation should be **suitable** to the profile, with the **rationale recorded**. Review the profile at least **once a year** or on a life event.

> **Exam tip:** Capacity, tolerance, required: take the lowest of the first two.
example: A client says she is aggressive, but she has a one-year goal and unstable income. Her capacity is low, so the advice must be conservative despite her stated tolerance.
say: I will record why each fund fits your profile.
Your capacity matters as much as your comfort with risk.
never: You said you like risk, so all in small caps.
We can skip the profile form.

check.why: Capacity is the ability to absorb losses.

check.q: When capacity is lower than tolerance, advice should follow:
check.why: Use the lower of the two.

check.q: A risk profile should be reviewed at least:
o: Yearly or on a life event
check.why: Review yearly and on major life changes.
